---
title: "R2 qwen3-14b-standard: coherent water check"
created_at: "2026-09-24T22:27:33+00:00"
status: unreviewed agent draft
profile: researcher
---

## Evidence for
1. [Study of Phase Coherence](https://waterjournal.org/volume-12/dolveck/): Simulated coherence domains in excited-state water, showing molecular orientation coherence across nanodroplets.
2. [GM-scale paper](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Dirk-Meijer-5/publication/321169214_Electromagnetic_Frequency_Patterns_that_are_Crucial_for_Health_and_Disease_reveal_a_Generalized_Biophysical_Principle_the_GM_scale/links/5a1309800f7e9b1e572c2eb8/Electromagnetic-Frequency-Patterns-that-are-Crucial-for-Health-and-Disease-reveal-a-Generalized-Biophysical-Principle-the-GM-scale.pdf): Geesink & Meijer (2016) proposed a semi-harmonic EMF scale correlating frequencies with biological coherence states.

## Evidence against
1. [QED model critique](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-8015/5/4/30/review_report): Reviewers noted the QED coherent domain theory remains controversial, with critical counter-arguments unaddressed in the paper.
2. [Simulation limitations](https://waterjournal.org/volume-12/dolveck/): Ground-state water coherence is computationally infeasible to simulate at scale due to molecular complexity.

## Most decisive experiment
The MDPI review (2024) highlights that the QED coherent domain model's lack of consensus in the scientific community, despite claims of establishing it as a framework, represents the most decisive counterpoint to its validity.

## Verdict
Confidence: 0.4. While coherence domains and GM-scale patterns are theoretically intriguing, peer-reviewed validation remains sparse, and critical skepticism dominates in established water science communities.
